text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein sponsors first conference of Arab political parties on Monday; prominent party figures submit working papers on important issues.
- Information Minister Muasher says "we informed Netanyahu of our deep concern over Israeli settlement policies", says Jordanian-Israeli differences "still large over many issues".
- Accord expected this week on electricity workers' pay dispute with management of Jordan Electric Power Company.
- Heavy rain falls on most of kingdom, floods in Hasa and continued cold spell.
- World Bank provides $120 million loan to Jordan to consolidate free-market competition and integration with global economy; loan is for 17 years with four-year grace period.
- Tunisian president to visit Jordan on Sunday.
- Release of first group of pardoned detainees arrested during civil disorders last August over bread price rises.
- Jordanians divided over separation of executive and legislative authorities.
